notice: Python and libraries on this page: the examples run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2 with Pillow 11.3.0 and Matplotlib 3.8.4 (the packages Pyodide offers), while the recording ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux with Pillow 12.3.0, Matplotlib 3.11.2, NumPy 2.5.4 and pyperclipimg 0.2.0; the results shown for the examples that run were compared value by value with the recorded ones, not as picture bytes. Thirty-one examples are shown as recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run, each with its reason: nineteen open the book's own picture and files from the zip of its online materials, which this page does not embed (their licence has not been checked, and that is an open question) and a browser cannot download; the others need a font file, a viewer, a child program, tkinter or the clipboard of the operating system, or print what a newer Pillow or Matplotlib says and the browser's older one does not. The other thirty examples were run in the browser and match. The pictures under ten concepts are the recorded ones made by the research programs; they were not made on this page, and no picture made from the book's cat or its logo is on it. Windows and macOS were never used. Virtual display: the clipboard programs ran on a virtual X display (Xvfb) and nobody saw the screen. The deck, whose text is the Lecture tab, marks slides 11, 14, 19, 21, 22 and 23 NOT EXECUTED (Windows and macOS, the Matplotlib window on a real screen, the pages and standards the study did not search, the commit the course pins and Python 3.14.7 and later), calls slides 4, 17, 20 and 21 Recorded (results of 13 October 2026 that it does not run again) and says on slide 19 that the clipboard program ran on a virtual display.
